title: Different domain mailboxes with same email contents.
creator: softrd
content:
I have three email accounts in thunderbird, each using unique domain names. I connect through a ProtonMail Bridge to my Proton account which is also configured with the three domains I'm using. Proton recognizes all three as configured correctly and if I send from any one domains address, all domain addresses receive it.

It appears things have gotten corrupted when I was doing lots of configuring and all my email inboxes share the same contents even though Settings->Server Settings->Local Directory is pointing to separate unique directories (the original ones) for each account.

Also, the "Drafts, Sent, Archives, Junk, Trash, and Outbox" folders are gone for all three inboxes (but exist for "Local Folders". The only "folder" under each account is "Inbox", and all three accounts (e.g. larry@a.com, curly@b.com, and mo@c.com) all have the same contents where every email from every account is all in the same Inbox. They're all mixed up.

I've not a clue what went wrong other than Thunderbird doesn't handle configurations well. I've tried the Inbox->Properties->Repair Folder to no avail. In fact, when I did that, it appears to have downloaded my main accounts inbox into the other inboxes possibly resulting in the mixup of email.

Thoughts?

title: Compuserve/AOL email account  access rejected after 153.3.1esr
creator: mark641
content:
Subject: CompuServe/AOL mail stopped working in Thunderbird 153.3.1esr — Yahoo says “invalid client id”

My CompuServe.com account stopped receiving mail in Thunderbird at approximately 1:15 p.m. Central on September 19, 2026. Thunderbird reports version 153.3.1esr, released September 18. I can still sign in and read the account’s mail through webmail.

When Thunderbird asks me to authorize access, I reach a Yahoo page titled “Review access details.” I check the box agreeing to the OpenID and OAuth terms and click Next. Yahoo then displays: “Uh-oh, looks like something went wrong. Please try again later.” Beneath that, it says: “Developers, please specify a valid client and submit again.”

The resulting URL contains `error=unauthorized_client` and `error_description=invalid+client+id`.

The incoming server’s authentication method is OAuth2. I checked that Thunderbird accepts cookies, and I have fully quit and restarted it several times. I have only one AOL/Yahoo-managed account in Thunderbird. My outgoing SMTP server is through a different provider and has worked in that configuration for years.

Could someone determine whether Thunderbird 153.3.1esr is sending a client ID that Yahoo no longer accepts, or suggest a way to restore incoming access without removing the account? I have not deleted or recreated it because I need to preserve my locally stored mail.
